newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to up gasoline prices 27 pct this month.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to up gasoline prices 27 pct this month.

text.p: The Venezuelan government will raise domestic gasoline prices 27 percent before the end of July, El Nacional newspaper quoted Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta as saying Saturday.
The increase, which would bring average gasoline prices in Venezuela to 70 bolivars ($0.14) per litre, will take place "after the 15th and before the end of the month," Arrieta told the paper.
The hike is considered central to an IMF stand-by agreement signed by Venezuela in April last year to bring fuels up to market clearing levels.
Congress is currently studying a new internal market law that, when implemented, would open Venezuela's currently closed retail market to foreign competition and market prices.
Gasoline price hikes are controversial in Venezuela, where motorists, long accustomed to subsidized prices, still drive gas-guzzlers.
Despite a nearly 500 percent gasoline increase last year, it is still half the price of mineral water and four times cheaper than milk.
